predecessors.name: Kanem–Bornu Empire
predecessors.text: Kanem, the Lake Chad plain north-east of the lake round Njimi (the page names Kanem and Njimi but gives no outline; the gazetteer region Kanem stands for it)

successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: The Yao sultanate: a disc of 40 km radius (about 5,000 km2, the page's 'area roughly 5,000 km2 in size' for the Bilala) round Lake Fitri; the centre is the researcher's approximation, the page gives…

ledger.x: Late 14th century: the Bilala rival the Sayfawa and take power in Kanem.

Late 14th century: Kanem passes from the Sayfawa mai to the Bilala (page: "captured the Sayfawa capital of Njimi and ousted the Sayfawa from power in Kanem"); same counterpart event as the empire-of-kanem dossier's 1380 loss, year not on this page.
About 1630: Wadai expels the Bilala from Kanem.
About 1630: the Bilala settle round Lake Fitri.

May 1909: the independent sultanate ends under French occupation (the page gives "independent... sultanate in the 17th-20th centuries" and no end year; the sultan of Yao survives as a traditional leader: Yao "is still the seat of the sultan of Yao").

wars.name: Bilala conquest of Kanem
wars.outcome: The Bilala capture Njimi and oust the Sayfawa dynasty from power in Kanem; the Sayfawa shift their base to Bornu.

wars.name: Wadai expulsion of the Bilala from Kanem
wars.outcome: About 1630 the Wadai Sultanate drove the Bilala out of Kanem; they resettled round Lake Fitri.

wars.name: French occupation of Lake Fitri
wars.outcome: May 1909: the Lake Fitri region, including Yao, was occupied and colonised by France.

certainty.note: The page gives Kanem and Njimi but no frontier; the Bornu dossier has the mai retaking Kanem in the early 1500s, so the Bilala hold may be smaller than the Kanem region.
The page gives only the modern area of about 5,000 km2 and the town Yao; the disc is a stand-in.
